Profile:
Skilled administrator and

SHANNON HAWKINS PERRY, PH. D.
Fleming Island, FL

recognized thought leader with 15 years executive experience in nonprofit and government sectors.

Passionate about leading and uplifting people for human services organizations that engage children and their families. Keen critical
thinking skills and high emotional intelligence allow me to create workplace environments that value inclusion, refine service delivery
for people in need of support, and build high-performing agencies.

Education:
May 2000 Doctor OF PHILOSOPHY IN SOCIAL WORK , The University of Georgia, Athens, GA 6
May 1994 MASTER OF SOCIAL Work, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, LA
May 1992 BACHELOR OF ARTS IN SOCIAL WELFARE, University of California at Berkeley, Berkeley, CA

Professional Experiences:
2/09 to 6/15 PRESIDENT/ CHIEF PROFESSIONAL OFFICER — Boys & GIRLS CLUBS OF NORTHEAST FLORIDA, JACKSONVILLE, FL

9/07 to 2/09 DEPUTY

Provided leadership and management of nonprofit organization which offered after-school programming
and summer camps to 3,000 children each year.
Coached and actively supervised the Directors of Club Services, Resource Development, Finance, Human
Resources, Data/ Support Services Manager, and their respective teams, which included 40 full-time staff
members and 125 part-time staff members.
Increased annual budget from $3.9 million to $4.9 million over a six year period, while guiding the
operations of [4 sites in Duval, Nassau, and St. Johns counties.
Guided the creation and execution of agency’s resource development plan which included goals and
progress toward attaining (1) foundation grants, (2) government grants, (3) in-kind donations, (4) major
gifts, and (5) special events. Presented to Board of Governors at monthly meetings.
Designed and spearheaded implementation of the B.O.L.D. (Building Our Limitless Dreams) Afterschool
Project which enabled the agency to assist an additional 250 children, to serve as a leader within the New
Town Success Zone Initiative, and to receive a $650,000 local government grant annually.
Routinely engaged in state legislative process and advocacy efforts with the Florida Alliance of Boys &
Girls Clubs to increase funding for organizations statewide and demonstrate retum on investment for the
Florida Department of Juvenile Justice.
Strengthened existing and developed new partnerships with other community-based organizations to
leverage additional resources and expand services.
Established junior staff’ youth summer employment program within agency, by serving on planning team
which helped design and implement United Way of Northeast Florida’s pilot Youth Employment Initiative
from 2012 to 2015. .
Led senior leadership team’s ‘successful completion of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America’s Advanced
Leadership Program and initiated internal training program.
Guided agency's effective involvement with Boys & Girls Clubs of America’s internal outcome study and
their external program evaluation of Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention federal grant
funding.
Worked alongside Board of Govemors to construct and implement programming at THE PLAYERS
Championship Boys & Girls Club in St. Augustine, which is a $2 million state-of-the-art facility (i.e.,
15,000 sq. ft.). Expanded the NFL YET Center in Jacksonville by building the addition of a $700,000
administrative wing (i-e., 5,000 sq. ft.). Also worked in partnership with the Boys & Girls Clubs of Nassau
County Foundation to implement programming for the Roberts Leaming & Achievement Center in
Fernandina Beach, which is a $1.8 million facility (i.e., 9,000 sq. ft.).
Advanced and supported the performance of Board of Governors with 20 to 30 members and promoted the
efforts of two Area Boards with approximately 20 members each.
Represented BGCNF in a leadership capacity on several councils and initiatives.

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR ~ CITY OF JACKSONVILLE, JACKSONVILLE CHILDREN’S COMMISSION,

JACKSONVILLE, FL

Assisted Executive Director/ CEO in leadership and management of public, funding agency serving 30,000
children with a $55 million annual budget and 95 full-time staff.
Coached and actively supervised the Director of Community Outreach and Director of Training and
Workforce Development and their respective teams.
Assisted in management of grant funding for primary services such as after-school programs, behavioral
health programs, early learning programs, and Healthy Families programs.
